questions.question: P is taller than Q and R is taller than S. If S is taller than Q but shorter than P and P is shorter than R, who is the tallest?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

1) P is taller than Q.

P > Q

2) R is taller than S.

R > S

3) S is taller than Q but shorter than P and P is shorter than R.

R > P > S > Q

Thus, R is the tallest in all.

Hence, the correct answer is **"R".**

Trigonometric Values at 45°

For an angle of 45°, both sine and cosine functions have the same value: sin(45°) = 1/√2 and cos(45°) = 1/√2.

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance of point **C** from foot **B** = 18 m

Distance of point **D** from foot **B** = 32 m

The angles of elevation are **complementary**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc8fbba9e2441773681de2aebd850aa1a33482a8c2473fede4707472b898665e.png] 

Let the height of the **tower** be **AB = h**.

Let the angle of elevation at **C** be **θ**, then the angle at **D** is **(90° − θ)**.

⇒ In right ▵ABC: tan θ = AB / BC = h / 18 — (Eq. 1)

⇒ In right ▵ABD: tan(90° − θ) = AB / BD = h / 32

⇒ cot θ = h / 32 — (Eq. 2) [Since tan(90° − θ) = cot θ]

⇒ Multiplying (Eq. 1) and (Eq. 2):

⇒ tan θ × cot θ = (h / 18) × (h / 32)

⇒ 1 = h² / 576 [Since tan θ × cot θ = 1]

⇒ h² = 576

⇒ h = √576 = 24 m

**∴ The correct answer is 24 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles

Two angles are called **complementary** if their sum is exactly **90°**. In trigonometry, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ.

Angle of Elevation

The **angle of elevation** is the angle between the horizontal line of sight and the line of sight up to an object.

Geometric Mean Property

In height and distance problems involving complementary angles from the base, the height is always the **geometric mean** of the two horizontal distances: h = √(d₁ × d₂).</p
